title: Tokenized feedback admission with regional fast-path and deferred degradation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a tokenized admission-control mechanism that integrates live feedback (latency & error burn signals) with per-tenant token budgets, a regional fast-path routing option, and deferred graceful degradation hints. The goal is to maintain SLOs for high-tier customers during multi-region transient overloads while maximizing overall throughput and fairness across tenants.
acceptance_criteria: 1) System enforces per-tenant token budgets and prevents burst overruns for 95% of tenants during simulated 3x traffic spikes. 2) Regional fast-path reduces p99 tail latency by >=20% for pinned fast-path tenants under overload. 3) Fallback deferred degradation returns partial or trimmed responses with clear response metadata for 90% of trimmed requests. 4) No regression in baseline throughput or p50 latency outside of overload windows. 5) Playbook for operator intervention and automatic reconciliation of token credits is validated in staging.
design_notes: We introduce a token accounting layer at the admission gate: every incoming request is scored by an estimated token cost (model variant, requested max_tokens, prompt length). Tenants have two token buckets: a short-term burst bucket and a refundable SLO credit bucket. Admission decision uses a three-way policy: allow (consume burst), queue-with-deadline (if burst empty but SLO credits available), or degrade (apply trimming policies or route to low-cost model). A lightweight regional fast-path flag allows selected tenants to bypass cross-region cold starts by prioritizing local capacity. Circuit breaker thresholds are additive: moving-window p95 latency, backend error-rate, and capacity occupancy. When thresholds cross, we switch to deferred degradation mode which annotates responses with X-Redwood-Degraded: reason and retained_tokens. KV-cache hits reduce estimated token cost and should bias admission to allow cached requests.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Admission layer prototype (token estimator + burst bucket) in canary runtime; feature flag gated. Phase 2: Integrate SLO-credit reconciliation and queue-with-deadline scheduler. Phase 3: Regional fast-path routing and fast-path prioritization queues. Phase 4: Degradation module to apply deterministic trimming rules and model downgrades. Phase 5: Circuit-breaker integration and operator runbooks. Phase 6: Staged rollout with synthetic load tests and canary by tenant tier.
testing_plan: - Unit tests for token estimator with diverse model/mode inputs. - Integration tests for burst bucket behavior and SLO-credit reconciliation (race conditions). - Chaos tests that inject regional outages and spike traffic; validate fair distribution and fast-path behavior. - Long-running soak to ensure credit reconciliation does not drift. - Synthetic mix that includes KV-cache hit patterns to validate cache-aware admission.
rollout_plan: 1) Toggle on behind FF in staging for internal tenants only. 2) Canary small percentage (1-3%) of production traffic for non-critical tenants in single region for 48h. 3) Expand canary to 10% with region-aware routing and monitor SLOs. 4) Add high-tier tenants to fast-path in paired region for 24h. 5) Full rollout region-by-region with 4-hour pause windows and manual operator approval checkpoints.
monitoring_and_alerts: - Alert: 'AdmissionCreditBurn' when global SLO-credit burn rate > 30% per 5m. - Alert: 'FastPathOverload' when fast-path queue occupancy > 80% and p99 latency > baseline+50ms. - Alert: 'DeferredDegradationSpike' when degraded response rate > 5% of total requests in a region. - Dashboards: per-tenant token usage, SLO-credit balances, queue latencies, p50/p95/p99 by region, KV-cache hit ratio, partial-response rate.
metrics: Primary: p99 latency, error rate (5xx + model errors), SLO-credit burn rate, degraded-response fraction. Secondary: tenant fairness score (variance of admitted throughput per weight), queue wait time distribution, cost-per-token during overload.
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Kickoff; spec reviewed with runtime and console teams. Added initial token estimator formula; agreed to use model profile table from model-catalog.
2026-02-27: Prototype admission gate implemented (FF=admission.tokenized.enabled); basic burst bucket logic wired into canary runtime. Observed expected behavior in local load test.
2026-03-02: Queue-with-deadline scheduler design vetted with SRE. Decided to cap queue length per-tenant and drop oldest requests on overflow to avoid head-of-line blocking.

2026-03-05: Implemented KV-cache weighting (reduce estimated cost by 60% on full cache hit). Running staging integration tests; found a reconciliation edge where SLO credits could be double-applied across failover—investigating fix.
open_questions: Q1: Should SLO-credits be refundable on successful early-complete requests that under-run their estimate? (tradeoff: accounting complexity vs fairness)
Q2: How aggressive should fast-path prioritization be when local capacity is limited but cross-region capacity exists? (tradeoff: latency vs inter-region egress cost)
Q3: What's the canonical response metadata schema for partial/truncated responses to support client-side fallback logic?
decisions: D1: Use conservative token estimator initially (round-up to 25% over expected) and iterate based on telemetry.
D2: Implement queue-with-deadline instead of unbounded queue to protect operator SLOs.
D3: Defer automatic refunding of SLO credits until reconciliation service is hardened; expose refund metrics to operators.
D4: Circuit-breaker will evaluate a compound score (weighted: p95 latency 50%, error rate 30%, occupancy 20%) to reduce flapping from single noisy metric.
